airports.name: Gimpo International Airport
airports.note: Domestic + short-haul international, closer to central Seoul

railNote: Dense KTX/SRT and subway network; every other region is reachable from Seoul stations within a few hours.
intercityBusNote: Extensive express and intercity bus terminals throughout the region.
localTransitNote: Best local transit in the country — subway, bus, and GTX commuter rail all overlap here.

railNote: KTX-Gyeonggang line connects Seoul to Gangneung directly; coverage thins out further south/inland.
intercityBusNote: Primary way to reach smaller towns not on the KTX line.
localTransitNote: Workable in city centers (Chuncheon, Gangneung); sparse in rural/mountain areas.

railNote: KTX stops at Osong and Daejeon put most of the region under 1 hour from Seoul.
intercityBusNote: Well-connected intercity bus network across all four sub-provinces/metros.
localTransitNote: Good in Daejeon and Sejong; more limited in smaller Chungbuk/Chungnam towns.

railNote: KTX/SRT connect Busan, Daegu, and Gyeongju to Seoul in under 3 hours.
intercityBusNote: Extensive network linking coastal and inland cities.
localTransitNote: Strong subway/bus systems in Busan and Daegu; more limited in smaller cities like Andong.

railNote: KTX serves Gwangju and Yeosu directly from Seoul.
intercityBusNote: Reliable coverage across Jeonbuk and Jeonnam.
localTransitNote: Good within Jeonju and Gwangju city centers; a car helps for smaller coastal towns.

airports.name: Jeju International Airport
airports.note: One of the world's busiest domestic routes (to/from Seoul)

railNote: No rail network on the island.
intercityBusNote: Island-wide bus routes cover most towns, but schedules can be infrequent outside Jeju City.
localTransitNote: Improved in recent years but still car-centric outside the two main cities.
